change: Append contiguous array slices directly from a retained source after checking bounds, with managed element retention. Matrix slice reads bulk-copy each row. Materialized self-append slices release their source snapshot before mutating the destination, avoiding whole-array COW detaches.
validation: Independent C bootstrap and full gate before the final self-append snapshot lifetime adjustment: 5263 passed in 148.12s.
After that adjustment: 670 focused numeric/slice/extend/reaction checks passed in 21.69s.
With an additional managed self-append/source-replacement regression: 48 extend checks passed in 4.17s.
coverage: Native/web, default/release; dynamic and fixed source arrays; open/inclusive/exclusive and empty ranges.
Source and bounds evaluated once before the destination; bound expressions can replace the source, and destination evaluation can grow a parent or change bounds variables.
No temporary slice allocation on eligible cross-array appends, checked during destination evaluation.
Nested managed values, saved independent copies, self-appends with/without growth, source replacement and repeated-work cleanup.
Negative, reversed and oversized ranges fail; fixed-array bounds fail before destination side effects.
Matrix ranks, slices and dotted updates; independent scalar simulation reference and renderer content checks.
limits: Runtime numbers cover the specific single-thread native workloads recorded in slice-copy-performance.json, not general program speedups.
Direct self-appends use a materialized selected slice; other aliases can still require a destination COW detach.
Matrix axis metadata and each output matrix are still allocated; this does not introduce persistent borrowed views.
Five compile-time pairs show no material regression on the selected workloads; absolute timings are affected by other machine activity.
